question: Which team will win the 2026 World Series?
title: The 2026 World Series
resolution: Resolves to the team that wins the 2026 World Series (best-of-seven). Game 1 was scheduled for October 23; this record is priced on the pre-Game-1 line and should be re-run once the series result is in.

consensus.headline_case: The Brewers are the favorite on the only price that matters, roughly 59–41 after the vig on the pre-Game-1 line, and the pitching and home-game arithmetic point the same way. Milwaukee owns games 1, 2, 6 and 7 under the 2-3-2 format.
consensus.why_over_runner_up: As single clubs, Milwaukee leads on the price, the regular-season pitching lines, and the home-game count. The Rays' case rests on one arm's postseason run rather than the series as a whole.
consensus.dissent: The Rays survived as the Talisman and Prophet case: Rasmussen's ALDS run is real and two first-time franchises make a story the crowd is drawn to. A split of the first two games in Milwaukee flips the read.

profiles.name: The Market Reader
profiles.criterion: Sides with the price the sharpest, deepest, most liquid prediction markets have set.
profiles.blurb: The Brewers are the price: DraftKings has them at −162 against the Rays at +134, which strips to about 59 and 41 after the vig. That was the pre-Game-1 line, and I read it as the market's verdict.
profiles.evidence: DraftKings moneyline pre-Game-1: Brewers −162, Rays +134 — roughly 59% / 41% after removing the vig.

profiles.name: The Quant
profiles.criterion: Trusts the mechanics and the models over recency and sentiment.
profiles.blurb: The pitching edge runs to Milwaukee: Misiorowski posted a 1.80 ERA in the regular season against Rasmussen's 2.67, and the Brewers host four of seven games. The model says a moderate edge, not a lock.
profiles.evidence: Regular-season ERA: Misiorowski 1.80, Rasmussen 2.67; Milwaukee owns home games 1, 2, 6 and 7 in the 2-3-2 format.

profiles.name: The Historian
profiles.criterion: Judges by counted reference classes — base rates, venue history, the record of prior cases.
profiles.blurb: Milwaukee's only Series trip was 1982, a seven-game loss, and this club has just swept the defending champion in the NLCS. The sample of teams that sweep a league series is small, so I hold the edge modest.
profiles.evidence: Milwaukee's only prior World Series was 1982, lost in seven games; swept the Dodgers in the NLCS.

profiles.name: The Path Reader
profiles.criterion: Ignores reputation and reads the actual route by which the outcome can happen.
profiles.blurb: Count the home games: Milwaukee has games 1, 2, 6 and 7 under the 2-3-2 format, which makes the route shorter. The Rays have to take three on the road, and that is the road I read.
profiles.evidence: 2-3-2 format gives the Brewers home games 1, 2, 6 and 7; the Rays need at least three wins away from Milwaukee.

profiles.name: The Talisman
profiles.criterion: Weights the elite individual — motivation, legacy, and the pull of the story the player is writing.
profiles.blurb: Drew Rasmussen threw 7⅔ no-hit innings in the ALDS opener, and he is the sort of arm that can turn a Series on one start. The story belongs to the Rays' pitching, and that is worth more than the moneyline credits.
profiles.evidence: Rasmussen's 7⅔ no-hit innings in the ALDS Game 1 win over the Yankees; 16-5, 2.67 ERA in the regular season.

profiles.name: The Contrarian
profiles.criterion: Favorites usually fail and the field is hot — hunts the underpriced live path the story forgot.
profiles.blurb: The favorite at −162 fails about four times in ten, and a Series between two low-payroll pennant winners is the kind of pricing that hands the underdog a real path. The Rays are the live leg the crowd is ignoring.
profiles.evidence: Pre-Game-1 Rays +134 implies about 41% after the vig; both clubs are low-payroll pennant winners.

profiles.name: The Prophet
profiles.criterion: Divine providence — backs the fated, story-shaped ending, however long the odds.
profiles.blurb: Read the story: two franchises still hunting a first title, and one of them has the arm that already did something no one expected in October. The omens favor the underdog's first crown, and I back it.
profiles.evidence: Neither franchise has a title; Rasmussen's ALDS no-hitter run is the omen the story is built around.

base_rates.text: Milwaukee's only prior World Series, a seven-game loss to St. Louis.
Home-field format giving Milwaukee games 1, 2, 6 and 7 — four of seven at home.

triggers: The Game 1 result: a Rays win in Milwaukee moves the band toward a coin flip; a Brewers win firms the favorite.
Starting-pitcher health and any late scratches in the Rays' rotation.
Two or more games at home for either side decides the 2-3-2 format's leverage.

method_note: Seven standing predictor profiles each committed to one club by a fixed criterion; the consensus was fused by grounding strength, with the strongest dissent preserved. The DraftKings pre-Game-1 moneyline is the anchor, vig removed.
honesty_note: The Brewers are the most likely champion at 55–63%, which also means the Rays win roughly four times in ten. Game 1 was scheduled for October 23 and its result could not be confirmed in this pass, so the price is stale until the box score is in.
